A 50-second instrumental track: the record a host has put on for friends at a dinner party at home, heard from a good speaker in the same room. A warm, mellow neo-soul / lounge-jazz trio, recorded clean and close: a Fender Rhodes electric piano with soft amp tremolo (chords on the first and fourth eighth of each bar, with a soft pickup on the sixth), a round, warm fingered electric bass on roots and fifths, brushes on the snare with a soft felt kick, played lightly, and a closed hi-hat whispering eighth notes. A simple, singable Rhodes melody in the middle register whose line falls E, E, D, B-flat across the four bars. Time signature 6/8, a slow lilting sway at 70 dotted-quarter beats per minute (one bar about 1.7 seconds). In tune at A = 440. Key: D minor (Dorian). A four-bar loop, one chord per bar, repeating the whole way through: Dm9 | G13 | Cmaj9 | A7(b9). Mood: easy, intimate, unhurried, a little bittersweet, friendly. Mix: warm, close, mid-focused.
[0:00 - 0:50] Already in full swing on the very first downbeat (no intro, no count-in, no fade-in): Rhodes chords, bass, brushes and kick, with the simple melody on top, at one steady level the whole way through, with only small variations in the Rhodes voicings.
Instrumental only, no vocals, no humming, no scat. Avoid: an intro or an ending, builds, breakdowns, drum fills, key or tempo changes, a heavy kick, synth bass, a saxophone solo, bright crash cymbals, elevator-music clichés, and anything dark, tense or cinematic.
